items.title: Lisa Parrott interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 22, 2021
items.q: we were like listening to the rhythm section’s albums — Monk, Miles, just all classic modern jazz stuff

ctx.x: So in your choice of tunes was there a balance between what you all wanted to play and what you felt maybe what we need to play?

The drummer, Andrew, had a massive vinyl collection. Now records in Australia were really expensive. A second-hand record was $15. So I never had a big vinyl collection so I had cassette tapes of people’s stuff. But he did. It seemed like always the rhythm section people could afford the albums and all the horn players, we were like listening to the rhythm section’s albums — Monk, Miles, just all classic modern jazz stuff. So we did a ton of like Miles sort of stuff. So it was a mix of like a lot of standards,…
I love that because you could form a question like, “Was it the higher pitch that just spoke to you that you wanted to go to the E flat horn?” No. My horn got squished.
